chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Thabit ibn Abi Safiyya, on the authority of Sa'd al-Khaffaf, on the authority of al-Asbagh ibn Nabata said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

God, the Blessed and Exalted, said to Moses (peace be upon him): 'O Moses! Guard my advice to you regarding four things: The first is, as long as you do not see your sins forgiven, do not occupy yourself with the faults of others; The second is, as long as you do not see My treasures exhausted, do not grieve over your provision; The third is, as long as you do not see the end of My dominion, do not hope in anyone other than Me; And the fourth is, as long as you do not see Satan dead, do not feel secure from his deceit.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four pieces of advice God gave to Moses in this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this divine advice to Moses, framing it within the Shia tradition of *tawhid* in action, where self-awareness of one's own imperfections prevents the distraction of judging others. The four conditions highlight the dynamic nature of spiritual vigilance, linking personal accountability with absolute reliance on God's infinite mercy and power over creation. This narration serves as a practical guide for believers to maintain inner peace by focusing on their own spiritual state rather than external circumstances or other people.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-41 Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qat’tan narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa’id al-Hamdani (al-Kufy) quoted Ali ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faz’zal, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Sabet ibn Abi Safiyya, on the authority of Sa’ed al-Khifaf, on the authority of Al-Asbaq ibn al-Nobatat that the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) said,

“The Blessed the Sublime God told Moses (MGB), ‘O Moses! Follow my advice to you regarding four issues: First, try not to find faults with others as long as you do not know whether or not your own sins are forgiven; Second, do not worry about your share of daily bread as long as you know that my treasures are not finished. Third, do not place hope in other’s help as long as you know My Kingdom is lasting. Fourth, do not feel secure from the plans of Satan for as long as Satan exists.’”
